title: Episodic traffic architect and shadow sweeper for model admittance
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Current canary mechanics move strictly by single-step traffic deltas and lack a lightweight probing mode that both validates quality and exercises KV/cache priming. We see flapping when traffic is increased quickly due to cold caches and cohort-specific regressions that surface only under small, episodic exposures.

Proposal summary: Implement an 'episodic traffic' policy and a separate 'shadow sweeper' probe. The episodic traffic policy advances traffic in discrete epochs (short, repeated exposures) rather than a single continuous ramp. Each epoch is followed by a short hold and aggregated signal evaluation. The shadow sweeper continuously mirrors a small sample of live requests to the candidate model and evaluates quality signals that are not covered by standard error/latency metrics (semantic divergence, hallucination heuristics, embedding drift).

Why unique: This ticket combines time-boxed exposure (epochs) with a continuous shadowing probe that feeds the same telemetry plane. The goal is to reduce false positive rollbacks caused by cold-start effects and to catch cohort-specific issues earlier than full promotion. It also clarifies how to compose episodic schedules with existing canary step schedules and autoscaler interactions.

Scope: runtime changes (policy compiler, new scheduler), console UI for episodic schedule authoring, telemetry dashboard additions, rollout safety checks, unit/e2e tests, and a migration plan for existing canaries.

Out-of-scope: model training, long-running A/B analytics (this is focused on admission gating and early QA).
rollout_config_example:
# Example episodic rollout config (YAML-like)
name: episodic-sweep-variant
description: 'Three epoch exposures with shadow sweeper active between epochs'
epochs:
  - id: epoch-1
    duration_minutes: 20
    traffic_percent: 2
    post_hold_minutes: 10
  - id: epoch-2
    duration_minutes: 40
    traffic_percent: 8
    post_hold_minutes: 20
  - id: epoch-3
    duration_minutes: 90
    traffic_percent: 25
    post_hold_minutes: 30
shadow_sweeper:
  enabled: true
  sample_percent: 0.5
  semantic_checks: [embedding-drift, answer-consistency, hallucination-score]
  cache_priming: true
abort_conditions:
  - name: p95_latency_regression
    window_minutes: 15
    threshold_percent: 25
    action: abort_and_rollback
  - name: error_rate_spike
    window_minutes: 10
    absolute_threshold: 0.02
    action: pause_and-alert
promotion_rules:
  early_promote_if:
    - condition: all_recent_epochs_pass
      required_epochs: 2
      action: promote_to_next_epoch_immediately
telemetry_and_alerts: metrics: runtime.p95_latency_ms, runtime.error_rate, runtime.cpu_util, model.hallucination_score, model.embedding_drift_score, runtime.kv_cache_hit_rate
alert: episodic.p95_delta > 20% for 2 consecutive epochs -> Severity: P0 -> runbook: Rollback-via-console
alert: shadow.hallucination_score > 0.25 over 30m -> Severity: P1 -> Slack #inference-ops
dashboard: Episodic Rollouts Overview (per-model) - links to /console/dashboards/episodic-rollouts
tracing: link to distributed traces for sample requests mirrored by shadow sweeper (/traces?tag=shadow=true)
test_plan: Unit tests for policy compiler changes (epoch scheduling, abort evaluation)
Integration tests: 3-epoch simulation with synthetic latency/error injection (CI)
Shadow-only dry run: enable sweeper for a non-production variant for 48h to validate semantic checks
Load test: replay production QPS at 25% traffic for 1 hour with KV cache cold/warm scenarios
Canary-to-epoch migration test: convert an existing linear canary to episodic schedule and validate rollback behavior
rollout_playbook: Step 1: Create episodic schedule in Console (use template 'episodic-sweep')
Step 2: Enable shadow sweeper with sample_percent=0.5% and run for 2 epochs before raising traffic
Step 3: Monitor p95, error_rate, hallucination_score, and embedding_drift dashboards every epoch end
Step 4: If abort condition fires, run 'redwood rollback model <variant>' and attach incident notes to the rollout job
Step 5: Postmortem: within 48h, log findings and decide if variant needs fixes or further shadowing
notes: Decision: prefer discrete epochs over gradual linear ramp for high-variance cohorts (retail checkout flows)
Tradeoff: episodic schedule adds longer total time-to-full-promotion but reduces noise-driven rollbacks
Design: shadow sweeper uses asynchronous mirroring with best-effort throttling to avoid additional tail latency on primary path
Operational: add quota guard to limit total mirror QPS to 1% of primary QPS to bound cost
acceptance_criteria: Policy compiler can ingest episodic YAML and produce per-epoch schedules (unit tests passing)
Shadow sweeper mirrors 0.5% of traffic with no measurable added latency to the primary path (<1ms median added) in canary lab
Rollback triggers correctly detect p95 and hallucination-score breaches and execute abort action in staging
Console UI exposes epoch timeline and allows manual abort/promote actions
Runbook validated by SRE during tabletop drill
